ai_summary: Markets+ proposes establishing a new Trading Hub (COLORADO_HUB) constructed via cluster analysis of 2025 WEIS LMP data. A Trading Hub is defined as a Settlement Location aggregating Pnodes for financial and trading purposes and must meet tariff requirements: sufficient nodes to calculate reliable LMP at all times, resilience to single-node or adjacent-line outages, high service availability, and relatively unconstrained transmission service among constituent Pnodes. SPP Markets+ adapted methodology from its prior RTOE Trading Hub analysis, applying unsupervised machine-learning cluster analysis to identify initial ten potential clusters, then refined iteratively to a single proposed hub. The Market Operator recommends establishing Cluster 1 from the 2nd Refinement (COLORADO_HUB) as a new trading hub on grounds that it meets all tariff requirements, exhibits LMP behavior comparable to existing trading hubs, and achieves optimal standard deviation and maximum distance among analyzed Pnodes based on 2025 LMP data.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage directly. However, trading hubs are the settlement locations at which hydro facilities' energy sales are priced by LMP. The hub's composition—which Pnodes it aggregates—affects which price signals hydro operators face, their hedging and trading options, and ultimately their revenue on energy sales. The cluster methodology determines whether nodes with similar LMP behavior (and thus similar hydro scarcity value) are grouped into a single hub; changes to hub structure could materially shift LMP volatility and spreads that hydro owners encounter in real-time and forward markets.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ Multi-Day Forecast Analysis (MDFA) is a non-binding, informational study performed daily after Day-Ahead Market clearing, covering the next 3–7 operating days and producing hourly LMP forecasts, marginal commitment and dispatch targets, and marginal GHG prices for all market participants and balancing authorities. MDFA uses Day-Ahead Market results as the anchor point, supplemented by roll-forward estimates of future resource offers, commitment status, interchange transactions, and flexibility reserve requirements when actual future data are unavailable. Outputs include hourly LMP forecasts and MCP forecasts (public), forecast commitments and hourly dispatch targets (market participants and BAs), and potential minimum/maximum generation and scarcity notifications (BAs only). Protocol changes (MIR40-R) clarify MDFA functionality and restrict minimum/maximum generation and scarcity data to BAs only, removing visibility for Transmission Operators and Reliability Coordinators. MDWG approval is scheduled for 7 October 2026, MORWG approval for 28 October 2026, and MPEC approval for 10 November 2026; comment period deadline is 23 September 2026.
hydro_read_through: The document does not address hydropower or PSH by name. However, MDFA directly affects use-limited resource planning: the 3–7 day dispatch and price forecasts enable hydro and PSH operators to schedule water release and charging cycles based on forward locational scarcity and demand signals, and the roll-forward methodology means early forecasts (day-ahead anchor + few days out) are most reliable while longer horizons degrade—a fact essential for water-constrained commitment decisions. The visibility restriction for minimum/maximum generation concerns to BAs only (removing Transmission Operator and Reliability Coordinator sight lines) may reduce hydro operators' awareness of system stress signals used to guide their own generation scheduling, depending on BA communication practices.

ai_summary: Markets+ will operate a daily Multi-Day Forecast Analysis (MDFA) covering the next 3–7 operating days, producing non-binding commitment, dispatch, and pricing forecasts for Market Participants and Balancing Authorities. The MDFA uses actual Day-Ahead Market results rolled forward as anchors for future days, supplemented by load and variable-energy-resource forecasts, with estimated inputs (interchange transactions, flexibility reserves, resource offers, and commitment status) rolling forward from Operating Day values when future actual submissions are unavailable. Outputs include hourly LMP and marginal cost-of-production forecasts distributed publicly via the Markets User Interface/API and SPP Portal; Balancing Authorities also receive forecasts of commitment, start/stop times, dispatch targets, and minimum/maximum generation concerns. The document notes that results depend entirely on input quality and accuracy and that market and system conditions can shift significantly over the 3–7 day horizon. MIR40-R (the protocol change documenting the MDFA) is scheduled for MDWG approval October 7, 2026, MORWG approval October 28, 2026, and MPEC approval November 10, 2026, with a comment period deadline to be announced.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage directly. However, hydropower and run-of-river resources are Market Participants subject to the MDFA's use-of-estimates framework and will rely on the rolled-forward offer and commitment forecasts to plan multi-day outages, fuel-use window timing, and ramping dispatch patterns. Because estimated inputs are based on prior-day actuals rolled forward without account for hydro-specific inflow variation, water-availability changes, or seasonal hydro conditions over the 3–7 day horizon, the forecasts will carry material uncertainty for run-of-river and seasonal-storage-limited resources; conversely, the non-binding informational status means hydro owners are not locked into these forecasts' implications for their energy and reserve offers. The key operational question for hydro operators is how they will use these outputs in real-time decision-making and whether the roll-forward methodology adequately captures hydro-specific risks (inflow variation, outage sequencing) that might make the forecasts misleading for operational commitment.

ai_summary: Markets+ Resource Hubs allow Market Participants to aggregate multiple Resource Price Nodes into a single Settlement Location, composed of any non-retired resources with which the participant is affiliated and spanning multiple Participating Balancing Authorities. Resource Hubs are registered via the Markets+ Registration Workbook, assigned weighting factors by the Market Participant, and settle at a weighted-average locational marginal price across their constituent nodes. The Market Operator must post approved Resource Hub establishment at least 45 days prior to effective date and approved termination at least 6 months prior; termination is blocked if the Hub ties to an active bilateral contract (Internal Energy Schedule Settlement Adjustment) unless both parties consent. Resource Hubs may support High Priority Seasonal Surplus sales (MIR 36.1R) or bilateral contracts. The mechanism is defined in Markets+ protocols but is not yet in the Markets+ Tariff; MIR 28 will add it.
hydro_read_through: Multi-location hydro portfolios—whether spread across balancing-authority boundaries or co-located with other resources—can use Resource Hubs to consolidate settlement into a single price node, simplifying accounting and enabling coordinated bilateral sales. Hydro's ability to weight nodes by operational or commercial preference (e.g., privileging high-scarcity locations) and to tie Hubs to seasonal surplus-energy contracts creates new value-capture pathways for seasonal and geographic flexibility that weren't previously available through node-by-node settlement. The 45-day and 6-month posting windows create forward-planning constraints that hydro operators will need to integrate into annual resource-planning cycles.

ai_summary: Markets+ Design Working Group presented a proposal to modify MTU and Schedule 1-B1 charge treatment for hybrid and co-located battery resources. Currently, co-located resources (solar + battery registered separately at the same point of interconnection) are charged on gross output of both components (solar output + battery input + battery output), resulting in roughly 3x the charges of a hybrid resource (where battery and solar are registered as a single unit and charging may offset generation). The document shows cost-impact examples: for a 100 MW battery cycling 365 times annually at 85% efficiency over 4 hours, hybrid registration costs $24,820/year while co-located costs $83,220/year; at 2000 MW scale, costs are $496,400 (hybrid) vs. $1,664,400 (co-located). The proposal is to charge hybrid and co-located resources identically on net output only. Next step is potential Markets Initiation Request (MIR).
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage. However, the metering and charge treatment for hybrid vs. co-located configurations sets precedent for how Markets+ would assess round-trip efficiency losses when any dispatchable or storage resource is registered alongside variable generation. A PSH facility co-located with solar or wind, or a conventional hydro plant paired with battery storage at the same interconnection point, would face the same 3x charge differential if registered separately rather than as a hybrid unit. The charge structure creates economic incentive to register mixed-resource facilities as hybrids rather than separate entities, which affects capital structure and operational bundling decisions for hydro operators considering such co-location strategies.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ is developing a functional design for Intermarket Optimization (IMO) to automate energy transfers between SPP and MISO in real-time, triggered when interface price differences exceed a hurdle rate (equivalent to applicable fees plus a predetermined risk premium). IMO operates on a 5-minute interval cycle: each market posts its real-time case results, the markets compare interface prices and decide whether to exchange power, and dispatch runs inclusive of finalized IMO megawatts. The MW quantity and direction of exchange (import vs. export) is determined decentralized by each market pair based on posted prices and information exchanged ex-ante; transactions occur every 5 minutes when price signals support them. Markets+ is identifying a single external interface point and considering whether to execute IMO-based transactions through a neighboring Balancing Authority System Point (MPSP), with questions remaining on whether transactions will be encouraged during excess capacity versus capacity-shortage conditions. The document notes potential production-cost savings from IMO of approximately $20/M per year based on historical price divergence from May 2023 to May 2025 at the MISO-SPP seam. Phases of implementation include Establish, Enhance, and Intra-Phase Evaluate. Open action items address interface definition, source/sink point identification, and operational impact on High Priority and Uncommitted Exports/Imports.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage. IMO's automated, real-time price-based dispatch coordination between SPP and MISO will affect how hydro generation at or near the seam competes with other generators for transmission access and market clearing. When interface prices diverge, IMO will move energy based on relative cost signals rather than traditional bilateral scheduling, changing the value of ancillary services and energy sales hydro operators can realize at the seam, and introducing a new layer of dynamic transfers competing with bilateral contracts and traditional interchanges for the same transmission. A hydro owner selling into or buying from across the seam must understand how the hurdle rate (fees plus risk premium), the 5-minute decision cycle, and decentralized quantity-setting by each market will affect realizable prices and dispatch timing.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ GHG Task Force met on 9/3/2026 to review accounting rules for Internal GHG Resources (IGRs) that are fully or partially contracted to serve load outside the GHG Pricing Zone. Current tariff attributes all dispatched IGRs to the GHG Pricing Zone regardless of contractual destination; the proposal would allow IGRs to indicate either a Maximum Attributed MW quantity or an Attribution Percentage, so that only the non-contracted-out portion receives the Marginal GHG Price and is attributed to the zone. Two implementation approaches were recommended: Maximum Attributed Quantity (MP submits max MW to be attributed; any dispatch above that threshold is not attributed) and Attribution Percentage (MP submits % of output to attribute; pro-rata impacts if partially dispatched). SPP staff will open a Markets+ Initiative Request to develop tariff and protocol language; default for all IGRs is 100% attributed, and fully contracted-out IGRs may indicate 0 MW or 0%. No specific registration requirements were recommended; the functionality would be managed through hourly offer parameters. Feedback should be submitted to Adam Cornelius at acornelius@spp.org.

ai_summary: SPP submitted comment MIR81-R proposing modifications to Markets+ Protocols (sections 4.1.4.4, 4.2.7 new, 6.1, 6.2, 8.2, 9.4; version 2.0a June 2026) to clarify e-Tag registration and BAA Scheduling Constraints for Market Transfer Interfaces and Market Opt-in Transfer Interfaces. The proposal distinguishes Normal versus Dynamic transaction types: Normal e-Tags submitted prior to day-ahead market clearance become fixed schedules post-Pre-RTBM SCED (30 minutes before operating hour); Dynamic e-Tags update via 5-minute allocations in real-time only. The objective is to allow participating balancing authorities to impose real-time BAA Scheduling Constraints that differ from day-ahead constraints without undermining the prior commitment plan, avoiding potential NSI (Net Scheduled Interchange) swings and binding constraints that could elevate prices. The MIR requires that MTIs/MOTIs defining a BAA Scheduling Constraint be of the same transaction type, and modifies transmission-contributor opt-in/-out procedures and congestion-rent eligibility verification timelines (15 days prior to calendar month, 4 business day verification window).

ai_summary: Markets+ initiative MIR8.1-R proposes to enhance Market Storage Resource (MSR) state-of-charge management by introducing time-coupled intervals in the Day-Ahead Market and RUCs, replacing the current design where participants must forecast state-of-charge for every interval. Under the proposed rule, the Market Operator will calculate state-of-charge by enforcing a constraint that the beginning state-of-charge for each interval equals the ending state-of-charge of the prior interval, ensuring commitment and dispatch decisions are physically feasible and avoiding conflicts between Day-Ahead Market commitments and real-time execution. hydro_read_through: Although the document does not name pumped storage specifically, MSRs encompass both battery and pumped-storage facilities registered under Markets+ protocols. Pumped-storage operators would benefit materially from this change: the current requirement to forecast state-of-charge for every operating hour of the next day forces PSH operators to predict market dispatch outcomes they do not control, creating either revenue-eroding overstatement of available capacity (to avoid infeasibility penalties) or unavoidable deviations from commitments. Shifting state-of-charge calculation to the Market Operator (through time-coupling constraints) eliminates that burden, allowing PSH to bid its actual physical constraints and respond to clearing without exposure to penalties for forecast errors driven by external dispatch decisions.

ai_summary: Markets+ Initiative Request MIR8.2-R introduces a Co-Located Resources Constraint mechanism allowing Market Participants to register multiple generating resources and Electric Storage Resources individually while designating a shared injection/withdrawal limit at their point of interconnection. The primary objective is to improve market visibility and functionality for resources co-located behind a shared interconnection; the secondary objective is to account for co-located resources in the Markets+ Must Offer Requirement. The market clearing engine will commit and dispatch co-located resources such that their collective output does not exceed the designated constraint, and can facilitate clipping between resources through market dispatch (e.g., directing a battery to charge before curtailing a variable generator if the battery's willingness to pay exceeds the generator's sale price). The design also introduces conditional treatment for Must Offer assessment: when co-located resources offer capacity exceeding the constraint, the Market Operator will use the lesser of offered capacities minus any MSR self-committed charging MWs or the co-located constraint. The initiative was recommended for Markets+ Participant Executive Committee (MPEC) approval at its August 2026 meeting.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower, pumped storage, or run-of-river resources directly. However, the co-located resources constraint applies to any Market Participant with multiple generators and/or storage behind one interconnection point. A conventional hydropower owner with co-located storage (e.g., a pumped-storage unit or battery) would benefit from market-based clipping — the constraint would let the market optimizer decide whether to charge storage or curtail generation in real-time rather than forcing conservative hour-ahead ECOL management. The must-offer treatment matters to hydro operators with storage: the design subtracts self-committed charging MWs from offered discharge capacity before comparing to the constraint, potentially reducing their assigned load obligation and increasing dispatch flexibility.

ai_summary: MIR9.2-R establishes a new resource designation (Dynamic Schedule Resource, or DSR) for Markets+ participants whose output is allocated to another Balancing Authority via Dynamic Schedule. The initiative standardizes treatment of Dynamic Schedules across five use cases: resource-coupled dispatches between participating BAs (dispatchable by Markets+, settled on dispatch/LMP); non-resource-coupled transfers (fixed in DA/RUC, included in dynamic NSI in real-time); resource-coupled exports to non-participating BAs (non-dispatchable, self-scheduled, settled on actual output); and non-coupled exports and imports (self-scheduled, settled as interchange transactions). A DSR must be 100% e-tagged with one Dynamic e-Tag plus additional Normal e-Tags, and is linked to a Dynamic Schedule Resource Interface (DSRI) that enforces power-balance accounting. MDWG approved the MIR on July 8, 2026; MORWG on July 29, 2026; MPEC approval is pending August 25, 2026. FERC filing follows an Interim Markets+ Independent Panel meeting scheduled September 28, 2026. SPP is tasked with enabling multiple DSRs to map to a single DSRI and multiple Dynamic e-Tags per DSR.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage directly. However, any hydroelectric or pumped-storage facility operating within a Markets+ participating BA and physically exporting energy to another BA via a dynamic interchange would register as a DSR and fall under these dispatch and settlement rules. In use case 1a (participating-to-participating, resource-coupled), the DSR becomes dispatchable by Markets+ in real-time, meaning the operator's dispatch commands supersede the facility's internal operations up to the Dynamic Schedule quantity — a material change from self-scheduling. In use cases 2a and 2b (exports to non-participating BAs), the DSR is explicitly non-dispatchable and must self-schedule, removing revenue optionality in the Markets+ market but clarifying settlement terms. The settlement treatment — settled on dispatch/LMP in case 1a, but on actual output in case 2a RTBM — determines whether the owner captures nodal-price risk or absorbs it. Facilities considering DSR registration must confirm which use case applies and negotiate e-tagging and normal-layoff treatment accordingly.

ai_summary: MIR60-R implements a Markets+ Interchange framework that defines Markets+ System Points (MPSP)—generic scheduling points within a balancing authority that facilitate interchange transactions—and Markets+ Interchange Transaction System Point Schedules (MITSPS), which are uncommitted interchange transactions sourcing or sinking at MPSPs. Each Markets+ BA must identify at least one MPSP, which will serve as source/sink for Market Transfer Interface (MTI) and Market Opt-in Transfer Interface (MOTI) transactions and external e-Tags, allowing the clearing engine to evaluate constraints on a BA basis. MPSPs are subject to Coordinated Interchange Scheduling Limit (CISL) constraints submitted by BAs, will settle at external interface locations, and are ineligible for virtual transactions and GHG attribution. The proposal passed all working groups unanimously: MDWG contingent approval on 07/08/2026, MSWG on 07/10/2026, MTWG on 07/27/2026, MORWG on 07/29/2026, and final MDWG approval on 08/11/2026; MPEC approval is scheduled for 08/25/2026.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower directly. However, MIR60-R reshapes how interchange and BA-level scheduling points function in Markets+, which affects hydro operators' strategic choices about participation, dispatch, and interchange under the Markets+ framework. ai_summary: SPP Markets+ proceeding MIR60-R establishes the Markets+ Interchange Transaction System Points Schedules (MITSPS) framework, defining how uncommitted interchange transactions (exports and imports) move across the Markets+ boundary using generic administrative scheduling points (MPSP) within participating Balancing Authority Areas. The protocol defines MITSPS registration, e-tagging requirements (requiring confirmed Normal e-Tags with OATT transmission between the boundary and the MPSP), and hourly interchange limits set by each BA. The framework applies to Day-Ahead and Real-Time markets and intra-day reliability unit commitment. All four working groups (Markets+ Design WG on 8/11/2026, Markets+ Seams WG on 7/10/2026, Markets+ Transmission WG on 7/27/2026, and Markets+ Operations and Reliability WG on 7/29/2026) approved unanimously with no opposition. The Markets+ Participant Executive Committee was scheduled to vote on 8/25/2026.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage. However, MITSPS enables dispatchable generators (including hydro) to schedule energy exports and imports dynamically in response to market clearing rather than relying only on pre-scheduled bilateral contracts — a significant operational flexibility gain if the resource can forecast its availability and manage transmission-rights management. For hydro plants with variable or seasonal dispatch flexibility, the ability to e-tag uncommitted interchange transactions into and out of Markets+ could open new revenue paths by allowing real-time or day-ahead sales to remote load, provided they can secure OATT transmission between their scheduling point and the boundary. The protocol's inclusion of MPSP limits in day-ahead and intra-day RUC inputs suggests these limits may constrain aggregate export/import volume at the boundary, which could affect the value of any individual export transaction if limits bind.

ai_summary: The MSR (Market Storage Resource) Subgroup update reports on the 2026 work plan covering five core design initiatives for SPP Markets+. Two priority design enhancements—MIR8.1 (State of Charge Management) and MIR8.2 (Co-Located Resources Constraint)—were presented to MPEC for approval at the August 2026 meeting. Three additional initiatives (MIR8.3 Hybrid Dynamic Limits, Hybrid Resources Holistic Review, and MTU Rate Design Review) remain in progress or on hold. On MPEC Action Item 61 (MTU rate design), SPP staff confirmed that Market Storage Resources and Co-Located Resources will be charged the Market Transmission Use (MTU) charge for all market activity (injections and withdrawals), at an estimated rate of $0.07/MWh. The MTU is a market charge assessed to all participants using the Markets+ footprint; FERC Order 841 addresses transmission charges, not market charges, so the MTU charge is compliant. SPP staff recommends closing MPEC AI61, and stakeholders may submit an MIR if they wish to propose policy changes to the MTU rate.
hydro_read_through: Pumped-storage operators will participate in Markets+ as Market Storage Resources or within Co-Located Resources and will pay the MTU charge on both charging and discharging activities, which is a new market-specific cost beyond traditional transmission charges. The State of Charge Management and Co-Located Resources Constraint rules (MIR8.1 and MIR8.2) are now moving toward implementation and will govern how PSH state-of-charge is managed in real-time dispatch and how hybrid/co-located resources communicate intra-hour availability constraints—directly affecting the optimization and revenue of PSH scheduling and dispatch. The Hybrid Dynamic Limits work (MIR8.3) addresses a recognized problem that hybrid resources currently lack a mechanism to communicate intra-hour availability, which affects PSH units that may be combined with variable resources.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ Initiative Request 8.2-R proposes a new participation framework for co-located resources (two or more resources behind the same point of interconnection) by formalizing a "clipping" mechanism that allows the market clearing engine to transfer MWs between a generating resource and a Market Service Resource (MSR) when the sum of their registered capacities exceeds their shared injection limit. The proposal adds a Co-Located Resources Constraint definition and modifies Tariff Sections 4.2.9, 5.1, and 6.2 and Protocols Sections 4.2 and 9.1.1/9.1.16 to require individual registration and separate metering for each resource, integrate the constraint into Day-Ahead Market and RUC clearing, and adjust must-offer obligations when co-located resources plus self-committed charging exceed the shared constraint. The MIR ranks as High priority with desired MPEC approval in Q1 2027 and implementation in Q4 2027. Design, implementation, and operational complexity are all marked as High. The change is classified as a "New Protocol or Tariff" introducing new functionality rather than a correction or clarification.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage explicitly, but it establishes the participation model for co-located resources that would directly govern how pumped-storage facilities and hybrid generation-plus-storage arrangements participate in Markets+ capacity, energy, and flexibility markets. Pumped-storage owners operating behind a shared interconnection point would need to register their charge and discharge functions as separate resources, comply with the new co-located constraint in dispatch and must-offer calculations, and could benefit from automatic MW-clipping to maximize revenue when injection limits would otherwise curtail generation. The must-offer adjustments for self-committed charging (reducing load obligation when charging MWs are co-located and exceed the constraint) create a new operational tool for PSH operators managing charge-discharge cycles around flexibility and capacity obligations.

ai_summary: SPP's Markets+ Initiative Request 8.2 proposes formalization of a 'clipping' mechanism and Co-Located Resources Constraint to allow energy transfers between co-located generators sharing a point of interconnection, improving visibility of injection limits and enabling dispatch of generation that would otherwise be curtailed. The rule modifies Markets+ Tariff definitions and Sections 4.2.9, 5.1, and 6.2, plus Protocols Sections 4.2, 9.1.1, and 9.1.16. It requires individual registration and separate metering for each co-located resource, while allowing their combined offered capacity to exceed the shared interconnection constraint; the Market Operator will commit and dispatch such that collective output does not exceed the constraint. Must-offer obligations for day-ahead and real-time markets are recalculated to account for the constraint, with special carve-outs when co-located resources include market service resources (storage) managing self-committed charging. The proposal reflects stakeholder input from July 20, 2026 (MRATF) and July 29, 2026 (MORWG and MSR Subgroup) meetings; submitter document revisions are reflected in April 2025 Markets+ Tariff and 2.0a Markets+ Protocols.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention conventional hydropower or pumped-storage facilities by name. However, the rule directly affects any hydro owner or pumped-storage operator that co-locates multiple generation or storage assets at a single interconnection point—a common configuration in hydro-rich regions where a facility may combine run-of-river generation with downstream PSH units or co-locate solar and wind at a shared substation. The clipping mechanism and constraint formalization change both how such an operator's combined capacity is registered and committed, and which MWs are available to bid into energy and ancillary-service markets. The interaction between the constraint and self-committed storage charging could materially affect must-offer compliance and revenue stacking for combined-cycle hydro-storage complexes, requiring close attention to how storage charging eligibility and exemptions are modeled under the new tariff language.

ai_summary: Markets+ Initiative Request 74-R proposes revising the must-offer ceiling language in Markets+ Protocols section 4.2.1 and Tariff Attachment A, section 5.1.1(B) to require that physical loads explicitly excluded from the Western Resource Adequacy Program (WRAP) forward-showing obligation be added back into the Day-Ahead Must Offer Ceiling calculation. The stated objective is to ensure comprehensive accounting for all loads in the Markets+ footprint and prevent unintended shifts of capacity obligations to balancing authorities or other market participants. The MIR identifies a compliance and reliability risk: WRAP-excluded loads currently avoid bringing corresponding capacity into the market despite still requiring service, creating gaps in the must-offer obligation during peak demand when the ceiling is most likely to bind. Submitter John McCoskery (Bonneville Power Administration, jwmccoskery@bpa.gov) filed the initiative on 3/27/2026 as an enhancement under normal resolution timing; desired approval and implementation timelines are TBD.
hydro_read_through: The document never names hydro or pumped storage directly. However, the must-offer ceiling is a critical revenue-protection mechanism for Load Responsible Entities and resource owners participating in Markets+. If a hydro owner or PSH facility is registered to an LRE or has contractual load obligations in the Markets+ footprint, tightening the ceiling by adding back WRAP-excluded loads would increase the amount of capacity that LRE must offer into the market, effectively raising the must-offer obligation floor and potentially displacing higher-margin self-scheduled or economic-offer energy. Conversely, if the change reduces the ceiling's scope of exemptions, it could improve the market signal for capacity adequacy and reduce forced-offer requirements during non-binding periods, benefiting flexible resources. The outcome depends on whether the submitter's concern about capacity shortfalls reflects genuine systemic risk or an attempt to relax incentive-compatible omission of use-limited capacity.

ai_summary: Markets+ Initiative Request 60-R establishes the Markets+ Interchange Transaction System Points Schedules (MITSPS) framework, enabling Market Participants to schedule import and export transactions at the Markets+ boundary using generic Markets+ System Points (MPSPs) as sources and sinks rather than specific resources or loads. MPSPs are scheduling points located within each Participating Balancing Authority Area that facilitate transactions into, within, and out of the Markets+ footprint. hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage directly. However, MPSPs will become a key pathway for any resource (including hydro) in Markets+ to sell energy exported out of the footprint or purchase energy imported in, functioning as the generic source/sink point through which boundary transactions clear in the Day-Ahead and Real-Time markets. Hydro owners who operate in or interconnect to Markets+ will need to understand how MPSPs affect their ability to export in-region generation to external load or import purchases, and how the BAA-specific interchange limits (which can be set hourly by each Balancing Authority) constrain their external-trade flexibility. The GHG non-attribution rule for MITSPS also means hydro exports through MPSPs will not carry forward source-specific emissions factors in the reporting framework—a design choice that could affect how renewable attributes or clean-energy program credits are tracked for hydro resources using this path.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ Initiative Request 8.1-R proposes to enhance the MSR (Market Storage Resource) design by introducing time-coupled intervals within Day-Ahead Market and RUC studies. The proposed mechanism allows Market Participants with MSRs to elect for the Market Operator to calculate State of Charge by constraining each interval's starting State of Charge to the prior interval's ending State of Charge as calculated by the operator, rather than requiring the participant to forecast and submit a State of Charge for each interval. The change is motivated by stakeholder concerns that the current design places disproportionate burden on MSR operators to predict dispatch and creates risk of infeasible Day-Ahead commitments conflicting with real-time capabilities, potentially causing capacity shortfalls and financial penalties. The proposal maintains the default policy that Market Participants manage State of Charge but introduces optionality to use market-calculated trajectories. Revisions affect Markets+ Tariff Sections 2.1.3, 2.2.3, and 4.2.2, and Protocols Sections 4.2, 4.3, and 4.4. The submission is ranked as High priority with desired MPEC approval in Q1 2027 and implementation in Q1 2027. Design, implementation, and operational complexity are all marked as High.
hydro_read_through: The document does not name hydropower or pumped-storage facilities, but MSR rules apply equally to any dispatchable storage resource in Markets+, including PSH. PSH owners benefit directly from this change because it removes the operational burden and financial risk of forecasting hour-ahead state-of-charge in their Day-Ahead offer when they elect the optionality—instead, the market operator will track actual dispatch and constraint each interval's state-of-charge to what was physically achieved in the prior interval, making their committed energy quantities feasible to deliver. This reduces the gap between Day-Ahead commitments and real-time capability that currently exposes storage to uneconomic dispatch or unearned start-up costs.

ai_summary: Markets+ Initiative Request 60-R implements the Markets+ Interchange Transaction System Points Schedules (MITSPS), creating a framework for generic Markets+ System Points (MPSPs) to function as source and sink locations for uncommitted import and export interchange transactions within and across the Markets+ boundary. MPSPs are generic scheduling points (neither resource- nor load-specific) located within Markets+ Balancing Authority Areas that facilitate e-Tag scheduling and tagging of transactions not pre-scheduled as bilateral interchanges but resulting from market clearing. The MIR amends Markets+ Protocols sections covering glossary definitions, offer submittal (4.2.2.7, 4.2.3.3), day-ahead and real-time market inputs (4.3.1.1, 4.4.2.1.1), congestion management (new 4.4.2.5.3), settlement locations (5.5.2.2, 8.2.6), and GHG tracking for import/export transactions (9.4.2). Participating BAAs may establish one or more MPSPs with optional hourly interchange limits (defaulting to 99999 if not submitted); MITSPS transactions are non-attributed for GHG purposes. Implementation is desired for Q1 2027, with MPEC approval targeted for Q3 2026. Design, implementation, and operational complexity are all rated as low; no separate impact analysis is required as the work was already included in the base Markets+ design.
hydro_read_through: This document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage directly. However, MITSPS establishes the operational and settlement infrastructure for interchange transactions that hydro operators will use to export renewable energy across regional boundaries or import low-cost energy during periods of constraint within Markets+. By establishing generic system points rather than requiring resource-specific tagging, the framework reduces administrative friction for hydro exports and enables participation in both day-ahead and real-time market transfer mechanisms — directly affecting the ease and cost of monetizing hydro's geographic location advantage and flexible capacity. The GHG tracking treatment (non-attribution of MITSPS transactions) will influence how Northwest hydro exports are counted under any future carbon-pricing linkages between Markets+ and other GHG programs.

ai_summary: Markets+ Initiative Request 60-R (MIR60-R), submitted by SPP staff on 5/29/2026, establishes the Markets+ Interchange Transaction System Points Schedules (MITSPS) framework. This MIR creates Markets+ System Points (MPSPs)—generic scheduling points neither resource nor load-specific—to enable Market Participants to schedule import and export transactions across the Markets+ boundary and within its footprint via e-Tag with confirmed OATT transmission. MPSPs will function as sources for export e-Tags and sinks for import e-Tags; participating Balancing Authority Areas may establish one or more MPSPs with optional hourly import/export/net limits (default 99,999 if not provided). MITSPS transactions are classified as Uncommitted Interchange Transactions, excluded from Market Participants' net position and must-offer obligations, and are non-attributed for GHG purposes (meaning their emissions treatment differs from source-specific exports). The framework revises Markets+ Protocols across multiple sections (Glossary, offer submittal, Day-Ahead and Real-Time inputs, settlement locations, and GHG tracking). Desired MPEC approval is Q3 2026 with implementation in Q1 2027. Design, implementation, and operational complexity are all rated Low; no separate Impact Analysis is required as MITSPS is already included in base Markets+ design.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage directly. However, the MITSPS framework establishes how generic system points facilitate interchange scheduling and settlement across the Markets+ boundary—mechanics that affect how any dispatchable resource or storage operator in the region manages bilateral and market-cleared export/import transactions, their settlement-location assignment, and GHG attribution. For hydro and PSH operators exporting across the Markets+ footprint, the treatment of MITSPS as Uncommitted Interchange Transactions (excluded from must-offer obligations) and as non-attributed for GHG purposes creates a distinct scheduling pathway; the optional per-BA hourly limits on net MPSP interchange may constrain export capability or create opportunities for intra-day flexibility sales depending on how each BA sets those limits.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ Initiative Request 8.1-R proposes to enhance MSR participation by introducing time-coupled intervals in Day-Ahead Market and Reliability Unit Commitment (RUC) studies to address reliability and financial risks. The proposal gives MSRs the option to elect, on a daily basis, that the Market Operator constrain state-of-charge within study windows to the calculated end-of-prior-interval value rather than relying on Market Participant forecasts. The change applies to definitions and MSR offer parameters in Markets+ Tariff sections 2.1.3, 2.2.3, and 4.2.2, and Protocols sections 4.2, 4.3, and 4.4. Desired MPEC approval and implementation are both Q1 2027. hydro_read_through: This document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage directly. However, the rule addresses Market Storage Resources (MSRs), a category that includes pumped-storage hydro and battery storage. The change would materially reduce the operational risk and prediction burden on PSH operators: instead of forecasting the exact state of charge at each interval (which physical and market conditions may render infeasible), an MSR owner could elect to have the Market Operator enforce consistency between Day-Ahead and real-time commitments by constraining state-of-charge to what the market actually achieved in the prior interval. This reduces the likelihood of over-commitments that would cause financial penalties or reliability shortfalls and shifts forecast responsibility from the MSR owner back to the market model—benefiting any long-duration or constrained-availability storage asset.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ tariff and protocols modification MIR9.2-R establishes rules for Dynamic Schedule Resources that are coupled to physical generation resources and export energy via self-scheduled dynamic e-Tags to non-participating balancing authorities. ai_summary: Markets+ has adopted a Revision Initiative Request (MIR) process (formerly called MRR) governing submissions, routing, review, and approval of changes to Markets+ Tariff, Markets+ Protocols, and the MIR Process itself. Qualified entities—including any Markets+ Market Participant, SPP staff, the Market Monitoring Unit, SPP Members, and governmental authority staff—may submit MIRs using an online submission form. All MIRs except those from SPP staff must be submitted via the Request Management System (RMS). Submissions must include submitter information, objectives (problem, proposed solution, expected benefits), identification of affected documents and sections, and proposed language changes if known. SPP has three business days to request additional information; incomplete submissions are not processed. Upon receipt of a complete MIR, SPP posts it to the website and distributes it within three business days to the MIR and Primary Working Group email exploders. The Markets+ Design Working Group (MDWG) is the primary responsible body for Markets+ Tariff and Protocols changes. The process includes a 15 business-day comment period before Primary Working Group review; comments must be submitted using the MIR Comment Form no later than five business days before the Primary Working Group's initial review. Secondary Working Groups provide secondary approval; all Secondary Working Group changes must be accepted by the Primary Working Group before Markets+ Participant Executive Committee (MPEC) and Markets+ Independent Panel (MIP) review. SPP conducts Impact Analysis (IA) assessing system, process, and staffing impacts, budgetary costs for implementation and ongoing operations, implementation timeline, and possible workarounds; IA results are posted for review, and SPP will issue completed IA within thirty calendar days after Primary Working Group approval unless longer review is warranted. The Primary Working Group may rank MIRs (high, medium, low) if they are more than Correction or Clarification, and SPP Staff schedules drafting based on rank, staff availability, and vendor availability. The Primary Working Group may approve (as submitted or modified, potentially contingent on IA review), reject, table/postpone (with optional additional 15 business-day comment period), withdraw, or refer an MIR. Primary Working Group-approved MIRs route to Secondary Groups, MPEC, and when necessary MIP. Process effective date November 13, 2025; document version 2.0 as of May 12, 2026.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage. However, this MIR process is the formal governance structure through which all substantive market changes in SPP Markets+ are proposed and decided—including changes to energy pricing, capacity accreditation, ancillary-services design, storage participation rules, and must-offer/operational compliance obligations that directly affect hydro and PSH revenue and obligations. Hydro and PSH owners active in SPP Markets+ need to understand the comment deadlines (five business days before Primary Working Group initial review), the routing path (MDWG as primary, with secondary groups and MPEC/MIP review), and the Impact Analysis process to anticipate when significant rule changes are under consideration and when comment windows open. Changes to tariff and protocols documents flow through this procedure, making it the chokepoint for all substantive market design that touches dispatchable and storage resources.

ai_summary: MIR81-R introduces a two-tier scheduling system for Market Transfer Interfaces (MTIs) and Market Opt-In Transfer Interfaces (MOTIs) in SPP Markets+. Normal MTI/MOTI flows, submitted by Day-Ahead Market close and used in the DA market, RUC, and Pre-RTBM SCED, become fixed quantities in the Real-Time Balancing Market. Dynamic MTI/MOTI, submitted only for RTBM, allows Balancing Authority Areas to impose separate scheduling constraints on the same transmission path in real-time without undermining the prior DA commitment plan. The proposal updates protocol sections 4.2.7 (MTI Tagging by transaction type), 8.2.1.1 (MTI Limit communication), 8.2.2.1 (MOTI Limit communication), 8.2.6 (BAA Scheduling Constraint timing), and 9.4.1 (MTI/MOTI registration requirements). Limits for Dynamic MTI/MOTIs must be submitted via the Market User Interface (MUI) and default to 99999 MW unless a BA-to-BA or TSP-to-TSP restriction applies; BAA Scheduling Constraint limits must be submitted by DA Market close but may be updated for RUC, Pre-RTBM SCED, and RTBM.
hydro_read_through: The document never mentions hydro directly. However, the mechanism matters for conventional hydro and PSH operators because hydro's value hinges on moving water-driven generation from run-of-river or reservoir locations to load centers via transmission interfaces. Locking in Normal MTI flows at DA-market close reduces real-time flexibility but protects the operator's commitment position; the new Dynamic MTI tier allows real-time constraint tightening on the same path, which would force incremental dispatch to occur at more expensive local generation or reduce the real-time price signal hydro captures on already-committed transfers. The BAA Scheduling Constraint update timing—now allowing updates post-DA and through RTBM—could create adverse real-time transmission congestion that was not priced into hydro's DA-market position, reducing expected revenues on fixed transfers or forcing hydro to curtail generation behind a newly binding constraint. Whether this change expands or constrains hydro's strategic dispatch options depends on how MTSPs and BAs exploit the Dynamic MTI feature in practice.

ai_summary: MIR82-R proposes to revise the Markets+ Tariff and Protocol queue-pause requirements for Transmission Service Providers (MTSPs). The current rule mandates that MTSPs pause all transmission service request processing between day-ahead market close and when day-ahead energy schedules are updated. The proposed revision allows each MTSP discretion to pause, limit, or otherwise manage queue processing according to its own operational requirements and procedures, provided coordination with Market Operator timelines is maintained and queue prioritization is preserved. The change responds to NAESB WEQ 001-4.13 timing-compliance concerns by creating operational flexibility for individual transmission providers. MTWG approved the MIR on June 25, 2026; MDWG approved on July 8, 2026; MORWG received it for education on July 29, 2026; and MPEC scheduled approval for August 25, 2026.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower or pumped storage. However, the change affects how quickly new interconnection requests can be processed immediately after day-ahead market settlement—a critical window for resources that may need to secure or adjust transmission service slots based on real-time dispatch needs. By allowing each MTSP flexibility in queue management rather than a hard pause, the rule could accelerate or smooth transmission service availability for generating resources including hydro, depending on how individual providers implement their procedures. The loosening of a rigid pause in favor of flexible, documented procedures may reduce artificial delays that could have disadvantaged use-limited or flexible resources seeking to optimize scheduling around market outcomes.

ai_summary: SPP submitted protocol change comments on behalf of the Markets+ Steering Working Group (MSWG) on July 15, 2026, to implement Markets+ Interchange Transaction System Points Schedules (MITSPS) and Markets+ System Points (MPSP) — generic, non-resource-specific scheduling points located within Balancing Authority Areas to facilitate interchange transactions into, within, and out of the Markets+ footprint. The MIR establishes that MITSPS transactions (imports and exports using an MPSP as source or sink) are classified as Uncommitted Interchange Transactions and do not count toward must-offer obligations. Interchange Limits on MPSP transactions (import-only, export-only, and net interchange) are submitted hourly by each BA via the Market User Interface and enforced in Day-Ahead Market, RUC, and real-time balancing market runs, with default limits of ±99999 if not provided. MPSP are used for administrative energy accounting and shift-factor calculations but have no associated market settlement; all settlement for MITSPS uses the External Interface Settlement Location LMP. The document proposes revisions to Markets+ Protocols sections spanning definitions, offer submittal, market inputs, congestion management, and settlement locations to incorporate MPSP and MITSPS mechanics into the day-ahead, RUC, real-time, and post-operating-day processes.
hydro_read_through: The document does not mention hydropower, pumped storage, or run-of-river resources. However, MITSPS and MPSP establish a new interchange pathway across the Markets+ seams that could materially affect how a hydro owner positioned in one BA exports energy to or imports from non-Markets+ areas (or other Markets+ BAs). The ability to use MPSP as a generic source or sink for scheduling and e-Tagging, rather than tying interchange to a specific resource location, could simplify hedging and arbitrage opportunities across the footprint boundary; conversely, the hourly MPSP interchange limits set by each BA create a potential congestion bottleneck independent of transmission capacity that could constrain the revenue opportunity from seasonal energy trading. The treatment of these transactions as Uncommitted (and thus exempt from must-offer) and the use of External Interface LMPs for settlement (rather than internal nodal pricing) are structural choices worth understanding as they affect how a hydro operator models the profitability of interchange strategies.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ has formalized the Revision Initiative Request (MIR) process, a unified procedure for submitting proposed changes to Markets+ Tariff, Protocols, and system enhancements. Any qualified entity—including Markets+ Participants, SPP staff, the Market Monitoring Unit, and governmental authorities—may submit an MIR on an SPP form to the Request Management System. MIRs are routed to Primary and Secondary Markets+ Working Groups according to routing criteria; the Markets+ Design Working Group (MDWG) holds primary responsibility for Tariff and Protocols changes. Submitted MIRs are posted within 3 business days and must receive written comments no later than 5 business days prior to the Primary Working Group's review. SPP performs an Impact Analysis assessing budgetary, implementation-timeline, staffing, and system impacts; the Primary Working Group ranks MIRs as high, medium, or low and may approve, reject, table, or refer them. Approved MIRs proceed through Secondary Working Groups, the Markets+ Participant Executive Committee (MPEC), and the Markets+ Independent Panel (MIP) for final review. The document (v2.1, effective 07/08/2026) reflects updates in response to comments by SRP.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ has finalized version 2.0 of the Markets+ Revision Initiative Request (MIR) Process document (effective date November 13, 2025, updated May 12, 2026). The document establishes the formal governance pathway for submitting, reviewing, and approving changes to Markets+ Tariff, Markets+ Protocols, and the MIR Process itself. Qualified entities—including any Markets+ Market Participant, SPP staff, the SPP Market Monitoring Unit, rostered working-group members, governmental authorities with SPP jurisdiction, and designated entities—may submit MIRs via the SPP Request Management System using a standardized MIR Submission Form. SPP reviews submissions for completeness within three business days and posts complete MIRs to the SPP website within three business days of receipt. Written comments on an MIR must be submitted using the standardized MIR Comment Form no later than five business days prior to the Primary Markets+ Working Group's initial review; all complete comments received in proper format are posted to the SPP website within three business days and distributed to relevant email exploders. SPP performs an Impact Analysis assessing budgetary impacts, implementation timelines, alternatives, interim workarounds, and system/staffing needs; unless greater complexity warrants, the IA is issued within thirty calendar days of Primary Working Group approval. The Primary Markets+ Working Group (for Markets+ Design matters, the Markets+ Design Working Group / MDWG) ranks MIRs as high, medium, or low and may approve, reject, table/postpone, or withdraw them; approved MIRs are routed through Secondary Markets+ Working Groups, the Markets+ Participant Executive Committee (MPEC), and where necessary the Markets+ Independent Panel (MIP). Draft MIRs ready for Primary Working Group review are posted for a 15-business-day comment period prior to the meeting; MIRs with shorter notice may be expedited or deferred to the next regularly scheduled meeting. This process applies to all Markets+ participant classes and replaces the prior Markets+ Revision Request (MRR) nomenclature.

ai_summary: Markets+ (SPP) is updating MIR9.2-R to clarify how resources that dynamically serve load in other balancing areas (Dynamic Schedule Resources) are managed in dispatch, power balance, and settlements. The proposal distinguishes resource-coupled (dispatchable by Markets+) and non-resource-coupled (not dispatchable) options across five use cases spanning internal dynamic transfers and export/import interchange transactions. For resource-coupled dynamic exports to non-participating balancing areas, the day-ahead and pre-real-time markets use the normal e-Tag energy profile as a fixed value and exclude the Dynamic Schedule Resource Interface, while real-time uses the Dynamic Schedule Resource Interface to set export quantity; settlements mirror this split treatment. The distinction between resource-coupled (dispatchable by Markets+, echoing output) and non-resource-coupled (self-scheduled with fixed day-ahead and variable real-time profile) models would be available to hydro operators choosing to participate in Markets+.

ai_summary: SPP submitted comments on Markets+ Initiative Request MIR9.2-R (Dynamic Schedule Resources), proposing tariff and protocol changes to clarify how Markets+ will process dynamic schedules within and across participating balancing authorities. The MIR defines Dynamic Schedule Resource and Dynamic Schedule Resource Interface constructs and specifies registration, e-Tagging, and ICCP requirements. Key proposed changes include: (1) requiring 100% of Dynamic Schedule Resource output to be e-Tagged with one Dynamic transaction type and zero or more Normal transaction types; (2) modifying the day-ahead market, RUC, and pre-RTBM to use the e-tag energy profile as a fixed value for self-scheduled Dynamic Export Interchange Transactions, with settlement at the external interface LMP; (3) in real-time, ignoring the e-tag in RTBM solution and instead using the Dynamic Schedule Resource Interface to set export quantity, with settlement based on updated Dynamic e-Tag. The proposed revisions affect Markets+ Tariff sections I (Definitions A, D, H) and 4.2.9, and Markets+ Protocols sections 1 (Glossary), 4.2.2.5.9, 4.2.3.3, 4.2.6, 4.2.6.1, 4.4.2.1.3, and 9.1.8. SPP stated this clarifies market processing, maintains balance without excessive regulation burden, decreases over/under commitment in RUC, reduces regulation burden on Markets+ BAs, and reduces the need to pseudo-tie resources between BAs.

ai_summary: Markets+ (SPP successor) is implementing MIR8.2, which adds a point-of-interconnection (POI) constraint for co-located resources (e.g., battery storage paired with solar, or DVER paired with MSR) registered separately but sharing the same injection point. This matters to hydro owners because zero-carbon hydro and pumped-storage assets will receive more accurate (and favorable) emissions-factor treatment in clean-energy programs and multiregional GHG accounting; the use of real-time heat-rate modeling and open-source peer-reviewed data strengthens the defensibility of hydro's zero-carbon claim in export markets and capacity-procurement contexts where GHG attribution determines eligibility and value. title: 05-MIR9.2-R Dynamic Schedule Resources June 2026.pptx  [in MORWG Meeting Materials 20260630.zip]
relevance_reason: MECHANISM: Markets+ Dynamic Schedule Resource rules establish how dispatchable hydro and other resources physically located in one balancing authority but serving load in another are accounted for in dispatch, power-balance settlement, and interbalancing-authority transfer accounting — directly affecting how hydro output is cleared, metered, and compensated across BA boundaries, particularly for multi-state/multi-BA hydro operators.
ai_summary: Markets+ proposes a new 'Dynamic Schedule Resource' participation type (MIR 9.2-R, June 2026) to solve a double-counting problem: when a dispatchable resource in one Balancing Authority (Native BA) is dynamically scheduled to serve load in another (Attaining BA), current rules treat its dispatch change in both the dynamic net scheduled interchange (NSI) and the market-to-interchange (MTI), forcing both BAs to regulate redundantly. The solution links a Dynamic Schedule Resource to a Dynamic Schedule Resource Interface; the resource remains dispatchable by Markets+ in real-time (RTBM), but only the interface value (not the resource's full output) is counted in the Attaining BA's power balance, preventing double-counting. The proposal defines five use cases: participating-to-participating BAs (resource-coupled or not), participating-to-non-participating (resource-coupled or not), and non-participating to participating. Most exposed are multi-BA hydro operators and pumped-storage facilities dynamically scheduled across BA lines; use-case 1a (participating-to-participating, resource-coupled) preserves dispatchability and shifts regulation responsibility via the interface, altering how dynamic hydro transfers compete in dispatch and how their locational and marginal-loss signals propagate across seams. Tariff and protocol sections are newly drafted; implementation timeline and stakeholder comment opportunity are not detailed in this presentation.

ai_summary: SPP staff proposes tariff and protocol revisions (April 2025/1.0a) to clarify registration, e-Tagging, and operational treatment of Dynamic Schedule Resources and Interfaces across Markets+ timeframes (DA, RUC, pre-RTBM, RTBM). The proposal distinguishes resource-coupled versus non-resource-coupled dynamic schedules and specifies when a resource may remain dispatchable under a dynamic schedule (internal transfers) versus when transactions must be non-dispatchable (certain exports). Key change: MSRs (multi-state resources, of which hydro is the canonical example) registered as Dynamic Schedule Resources can represent import or export depending on dispatch, but must coordinate separate e-Tags with the Native and Attaining BAs and accept ICCP-reported real-time quantities as fixed; Dynamic e-Tags referencing these resources are ignored by settlements, shifting compliance burden to the Market Participant. This reduces regulation burden on receiving BAs by eliminating pseudo-ties but locks the Dynamic Schedule Resource's output into the native BA's power balance and removes it from real-time economic dispatch in the attaining BA—a material constraint for hydro operators managing multi-BA export strategies. Status: tariff/protocol revisions have been proposed; next step and comment deadline are not stated in this excerpt.

ai_summary: Markets+ (SPP's combined market and reliability coordinator) is adopting a new registration pathway (MIR 9.3-R) that allows external resources physically located in non-participating balancing authorities to be modeled as pseudo-tied within Markets+ using dynamic schedules instead of formal NAESB pseudo-tie agreements. External resources registered under this new option will be dispatchable by Markets+, settled at their physical-location LMP, and participate identically to formally pseudo-tied resources, but the underlying dynamic schedule between native and attaining balancing authorities will remain in place (and ignored by the market system and settlements). The change preserves all formal pseudo-tie requirements and adds two new attributes: the market participant must designate the resource as a "dynamically scheduled pseudo-tie" in the registration workbook, and the participating attaining BA must provide an attestation letter confirming its understanding that the resource will be modeled as pseudo-tied. This creates operational flexibility for BA arrangements that cannot or prefer not to establish formal pseudo-ties, potentially broadening external-resource participation. The document shows protocol language updates to sections 9.1.1, 9.1.9, 9.1.9.1, and 9.1.9.2 but states no vote date or comment deadline.

title: 08-MIR81-R Dynamic MTI-MOTI in RTBM.pptx  [in MORWG Meeting Materials 20260630.zip]

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ proposes MIR81-R, which distinguishes Normal (day-ahead/RUC/pre-RTBM) and Dynamic (real-time only) MTI/MOTI transaction types to allow balancing authorities to set different scheduling constraints in RTBM than were used in DA commitment, preventing large NSI swings without undermining DA/RUC optimization. This affects real-time dispatch optimization and price formation: by allowing separate constraints for incremental transfers, the scheme constrains BAA scheduling-constraint binding in RTBM while preserving DA-cleared transfers, potentially reducing real-time price separation and limiting the incremental scarcity premiums hydro can capture on flexible ramping in congested intervals. All market participants must submit Normal MTIs/MOTIs prior to DA market close and register at least one Dynamic MTI at resource registration.

title: 09-10-MIR8.1 and MIR8.2 Update to MORWG June 2026.pptx  [in MORWG Meeting Materials 20260630.zip]
relevance_reason: MIR8.1 restructures how pumped-storage and battery resources manage state-of-charge forecasting across Markets+ unit-commitment studies, shifting from market-participant prediction to market-operator calculation of SOC trajectories — a material change to how storage revenue exposure and dispatch predictability are handled under Markets+ rules.
ai_summary: Markets+ MIR8.1 proposes to introduce time-coupled intervals in all unit-commitment studies (Day-Ahead Market, Day-Ahead RUC, Intra-Day RUC, and Short-Term RUC), allowing market operators to calculate state-of-charge for all intervals after the first, rather than requiring market participants to submit a SOC forecast for every interval. The change is optional: participants can elect either the current design (submitting SOC forecast for each interval) or the new coupled design (submitting SOC forecast only for the first interval, letting the market operator time-couple and calculate subsequent SOC values). The proposal targets a FERC filing timeline, with MPEC approval targeted for August 2026. For pumped-storage owners, this addresses a key exposure: misforecasting dispatch leads to infeasible SOC trajectories in real-time, triggering capacity shortfalls and financial penalties; time-coupling within studies mitigates that risk by ensuring the market solver respects physical charging/discharging constraints. The optionality preserves flexibility for hybrid resources and those charging/discharging outside the market (where the operator lacks full visibility). MORWG convened June 30, 2026; MPEC approval is scheduled August 25, 2026.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ is revising the OASIS Queue Pause design (MIR82-R) to allow individual Transmission Service Providers (MTSPs) to pause, limit, or manage transmission-service requests flexibly — rather than mandate a uniform pause — during the window between Day-Ahead Market close and Energy Schedule updates. Hydro operators in SPP Markets+ should assess whether the proposed flexibility in queue management creates new opportunities or risks for intra-day transmission-service requests (e.g., for storage recharge or ramping adjustments) or whether MTSP-specific procedures may disadvantage certain resource types.

ai_summary: SPP Markets+ releases Version 0.2 of its Interchange Scheduling Reference Manual (June 8, 2026), a procedural guide for energy transfers crossing Markets+ participating balancing authority areas. No formal vote or comment deadline is stated; next steps include SPP identifying meter agents and market participants by settlement area, distributing spreadsheet templates and exercise intervals in July, and scheduling settlement-area meetings for August.
